item.title: Epidemiological modeling in the age of artificial intelligence
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01070-1

Artificial intelligence is enabling epidemic models to learn across outbreaks. The next challenge is ensuring that these models learn and transfer not mere statistical patterns, but epidemiological mechanisms.
item.dc:title: Epidemiological modeling in the age of artificial intelligence
item.dc:creator: Max S. Y. Lau
Matthew J. Ferrari
Wei Jin

item.title: Photonic circuits become trainable AI hardware
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01071-0

A physics-based in situ learning method is demonstrated that directly measures optical gradients with photonic integrated circuits, allowing diverse circuit topologies to be trained after fabrication. This hardware achieves matrix design, multiwavelength computation and rapid meta-learning without requiring a full digital model of the circuit.
item.dc:title: Photonic circuits become trainable AI hardware

item.title: Steering complex rhythms
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01064-z

A recent study reports a property-first computational strategy, identifying coordinated parameter changes that can tune several features of a complex oscillator at the same time.
item.dc:title: Steering complex rhythms
item.dc:creator: Fan Jin

item.title: Advancing chemical reaction prediction in data-scarce drug discovery with active and geometric deep learning
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01063-0

Researchers pair active learning with geometric deep learning to predict the outcome and site selectivity of chemical reactions from scarce data, guiding experiments that accelerate drug discovery and expand accessible chemical space.
item.dc:title: Advancing chemical reaction prediction in data-scarce drug discovery with active and geometric deep learning
